image_description: A close-up studio shot of a bicycle disc brake assembly against a white background. The image features a metallic, cross-drilled rotor (disc) with a wavy outer edge, mounted to a central hub. A black and silver caliper mechanism is mounted over the top-left portion of the rotor. A black fork leg with 'SRAM' branding is visible on the left side, connecting to the axle area.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Circular metal rotor (disc), notably larger in diameter than its thickness.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The rotor is clearly circular and thin relative to its diameter, matching the geometric description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Caliper is cast metal mounted over rotor edge.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A mechanical housing (caliper) is visibly straddling the upper-left quadrant of the rotor's circumference.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Rotor is mounted to wheel hub with visible lug bolt pattern.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: While mounted to a hub/axle interface, the specific 'lug bolt pattern' typical of automotive brakes is not present; bicycle hubs use different mounting standards (e.g., Centerlock or 6-bolt), and the specific bolts are obscured or not distinct in this view.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Rotor is ventilated (two plates with cooling fins) or solid.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The rotor appears to be a solid single-piece steel disc with cutouts for weight reduction/cooling, which fits the 'solid' criteria.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Brake pads are rectangular friction material blocks pressing against rotor faces.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The internal brake pads are housed within the caliper and are not directly visible from this external angle.
No hydraulic hose or line is visible entering the caliper body in this cropped frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Surface shows machined concentric grooves or cross-drilled holes.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The rotor surface clearly exhibits a pattern of circular cross-drilled holes.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Surface exhibits heat discoloration (blue/brown tint) from use.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The metal surfaces appear clean and uniformly silver/grey, lacking the characteristic blueing or browning of heat-stressed used brakes.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Caliper is cast aluminum or iron.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The caliper housing has the visual texture and finish consistent with cast or machined aluminum alloy.

artifact_observations.location: Black fork leg on the left side
artifact_observations.reasoning: The white text on the black fork leg attempts to spell 'SRAM' but the letters are slightly malformed and irregular, typical of AI-generated text artifacts where character geometry is approximated rather than rendered precisely.

The connection between the caliper body and the fork mount lacks clear mechanical definition; the metal seems to blend slightly without distinct bolts or separation lines, suggesting minor structural ambiguity.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific type of braking system (bicycle vs automotive) and verify class alignment.
To check for edge bleeding or fusion between the moving rotor and the static caliper/fork.
To rigorously evaluate the legibility and correctness of the 'SRAM' logo text.
To assess the realism of the metallic reflections and machining details on the rotor.

focus_areas: Text legibility on the fork leg
Mechanical connectivity of the caliper to the fork
Edge sharpness between rotor and background
Realism of drilled hole patterns on the rotor
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the text on the left fork leg; AI often struggles with specific brand logos. Also, verify if the caliper mounting hardware is physically plausible or if it melts into the fork structure. The rotor holes should be uniform; check for warping or irregular spacing.
